result.title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
result.comment: A novel method for multi-agent system harness joint evolution
result.summary: AI agents can evolve by using environment feedback to revise their harnesses, the software managing model inputs, tool use, memory, and execution, while keeping foundation models frozen. Existing studies focus on single agents, leaving joint harness evolution in multi-agent systems (MAS) underexplored. A single global optimizer faces growing context and workload as the system scales, while access restrictions may prevent sharing agent internals or system-wide feedback. We propose HarnessNet, a framework for hierarchical harness evolution in MAS. Its basic unit, Agentron, comprises an evolvable forward harness, a foundation model, and a local optimizer that can observe and modify only that harness. Agentrons form a layered graph through which environment feedback propagates backward, with upstream optimizers receiving node-specific feedback from the downstream layer. This decomposes joint harness evolution into smaller, coordinated tasks with separate contexts, reducing individual optimizers' context and workload while keeping access local. Optimizers need not access all agent trajectories or raw environment feedback. Experiments on AgentBench with multiple foundation models demonstrate the feasibility of training HarnessNet. Compared with a single global optimizer, HarnessNet achieves comparable performance gains while respecting local privacy and requiring fewer tokens and less time per optimizer call. A migration study shows that the evolved harnesses remain jointly effective after replacing the foundation models, suggesting transferability across models.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 HarnessNet，把多智能体系统中的 harness 演化分解为分层图：基本单元 Agentron 由可演化的 forward harness、冻结的基础模型和只能观测并修改本地 harness 的优化器组成，环境反馈自下游向上游逐层回传节点级信号，并在 AgentBench 上验证了可行性、成本与跨模型迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反馈沿分层图反向传播＋各优化器只持有局部上下文」的机制，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态更新的贡献分配与监督分解提供借鉴线索，可供核查反馈粒度与信用分配方式是否可迁移；但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
